decisive_items: brown, multilobular lesions confined to the deep corneal stroma
central infiltrate involving all corneal layers and a peripheral infiltrate concentrated in the deep stroma
no conjunctival hyperemia, no discharge, no epithelial defect
response.rationale: Brown multilobular deep stromal lesions with intact epithelium and layered infiltrate favor fungal keratitis; prior Thaumetopoea infection had resolved and would not reactivate with this phenotype, while bacterial/Acanthamoeba typically show epithelial defects or pain.

rejected.why: Prior pityocampa infection resolved before surgery; current presentation lacks acute inflammatory signs and epithial defect, making reactivation unlikely.
Immune-mediated keratitis is nonspecific and not supported by distinctive deep lobular lesions or absence of epithelial defect.
Acanthamoeba typically causes severe pain and epithelial irregularities; no contact lens use or pain cited.
Steroid-induced keratitis is a mechanism, not a distinct diagnosis; no supporting characteristic lesions.
Bacterial keratitis usually presents with epithelial defect and purulent discharge, absent here.
